newsitem.title: USA: Suit against Chicago-Gary airport pact dismissed.
newsitem.headline: Suit against Chicago-Gary airport pact dismissed.

text.p: A federal court judge has dismissed a lawsuit brought by Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar that sought to nullify a pact between Chicago and Gary, Ind. that created a regional airport authority.
U.S. District Court Judge Harry Leinenweber on September 27 rejected the state's claim the airport agreement violated the U.S. Constitution and federal law, according to Chicago's law department.
Edgar filed the lawsuit in July 1995.

A spokesman for the Illinois Attorney General's Office was not available to comment on the lawsuit's dismissal. The Chicago Tribune on Sunday reported that the office was reviewing options for appealing the decision.

Chicago entered into an agreement with Gary in April 1995 to form a regional airport authority that had no ownership role in any of the cities' airports, but stressed instead cooperation on aviation issues.
The pact was sparked by attempts in the Illinois General Assembly to create a state-run authority to own and operate Chicago's O'Hare International and Midway airports.
Chicago officials warned at that time such a move could result in a material default on billions of dollars of outstanding airport bonds.
